## Bored Panda violates privacy and data laws
Bored Panda does not give users real control over their own content.

I posted work on their platform years ago. Recently, I decided to remove my content and account and was genuinely shocked to find there is no functional way to do it. There is no option to edit or delete your own posts, and when I contacted them directly, they ignored multiple requests.

This isn’t just frustrating, it’s a serious issue. They continue to display and benefit from my copyrighted images while refusing to respond to removal requests. There is a clear lack of transparency and accountability in how they handle user content and personal data. [...] EDITED TO ADD POST BORED PANDA REPLY: it took a complaint to Lithuanian State Data Protection Agency, a GDPR Complaint to the EU, Emails to their Legal Team (Ignored) Editors (Ignored) Privacy Team (Ignored) and a Trust Pilot review to get my account removed. And they still never replied to my emails. Only this review. Make no mistake, my emails weren't "missed" and if Bored Panda truly respected the rights of creators, they will CLEARLY and PLAINLY include instructions on how to delete accounts instead of literally disabling the delete function and ignoring emails to do so. I would recommend to save yourself the headache if you ever want control of your work and just don't publish there.
